proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 8 gives us Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity but nothing for Commerce One's breach of law, unauthorized disclosure of our or our Customers' data, or its gross negligence or wilful misconduct, so we have added those limbs (using the same notice, control and cooperation procedure) as required by our indemnity position. If Commerce One prefers, we can accept the IP indemnity alone only where its indemnity obligations are backed by a super-cap of 3x annual fees.

ops.text: 8.3 Additional Indemnities. Commerce One shall further indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio, its affiliates and its Customers from and against any and all third-party claims, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) Commerce One's breach of applicable law; (ii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Corio's or its Customers' data or Confidential Information caused by Commerce One; or (iii) Commerce One's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The notice, control and cooperation procedures set forth in Section 8.1 shall apply to any claim under this Section 8.3, and the limitations set forth in Section 8.2 shall not apply to this Section 8.3.

proposal.summary: Add Commerce One indemnity limbs for breach of law, data/Confidential Information breach, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct

quote: 8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
rationale: Section 8.1 gives us a Commerce One IP infringement indemnity with defence, notice/control/cooperation procedure and procure/modify/refund remedies, and Section 9 expressly carves Section 8 out of the liability cap, so the fallback is met and there is no reciprocal indemnity from us to narrow. However, the preferred position also requires Vendor indemnities for breach of applicable law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of our (and our Customers') data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct; those limbs are absent, so we inserted a new Section 8.3 carrying them and applying the existing Section 8.1 procedure while confirming the IP-specific exclusions in 8.2 do not apply.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the carve-out that would hand Commerce One ownership of Developments created solely by Corio merely because Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, and added a short confirmation that Corio and its Customers retain all rights in Customer Data with no assignment to Commerce One and no joint ownership. Our position is that we own what we build and pay for while Commerce One keeps its pre-existing Software rights (Section 2.8); if ongoing support is the concern, we can instead grant Commerce One a licence to the relevant Developments for support purposes.

rationale: Section 13.5 correctly gives us ownership of Developments (software interface coding and programs created solely by Corio) and includes an assignment from Commerce One, but the carve-out flips ownership of our own work product to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports those Developments on an ongoing basis. That is an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor, which is our walk-away position, and support arrangements should be handled by licence rather than title. The agreement also contains no statement that we and our Customers retain rights in data hosted on the Corio Servers or passing through the MarketSite.net Service (Section 10 only cross-refers to an NDA), so we added a short Customer Data ownership and no-joint-ownership confirmation. proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have set the cap at the greater of twelve (12) months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, applied to aggregate liability under the Agreement rather than only the amount actually paid for the single "transaction" at issue, which would make the cap illusory for most claims. We have also confirmed that indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and that Corio's fee payment obligations are not capped damages; a mutual 12-month fees cap with at least indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct carve-outs is our fallback.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS (US$1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 8, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. CORIO'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION AND SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES FOR PURPOSES OF THIS SECTION 9.
ops.oldText: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.

proposal.summary: Make cap the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000 on an aggregate basis, and add standard uncapped Excluded Claims.

quote: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
rationale: Section 9 is nominally mutual and excludes consequential damages mutually, and Section 8 (Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity) sits outside the cap. However the cap basis deviates from the playbook: it is limited to amounts "ACTUALLY PAID" by Corio and only for "THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO", so it is neither an aggregate 12-month fees cap nor subject to the USD 1,000,000 floor, and it is illusory where little has yet been paid for the specific transaction (e.g. early-term or revenue-share fees under Exhibit B). Carve-outs are also incomplete: only Section 8 indemnity is excluded, with nothing for confidentiality (Section 10), data/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud or infringement of the other party's IP, and Corio's fee payment obligations are not carved out of the cap/damages concept. Redline changes the basis to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000 on an aggregate basis and adds a single "Excluded Claims" sentence, leaving the mutual consequential-damages exclusion untouched.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate, applied a "not unreasonably withheld" standard to consent, and limited the competitor restriction so it applies to Commerce One's assignments rather than blocking our own merger or asset sale. Our playbook requires that a corporate transaction on our side not be conditioned on the other party's consent; if helpful, we can accept a mutual notice-based successor assignment right as a fallback.

ops.newText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Notwithstanding the foregoing, (a) Corio shall have the right to assign this Agreement, without such consent, to any entity that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with Corio, and (b) either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except that Commerce One may not assign this Agreement to a direct competitor of Corio without Corio's prior written consent.
ops.oldText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate assignment right for Corio, a reasonableness standard on consent, and limit the competitor carve-back to Commerce One assignments.

quote: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
rationale: Section 14.1 is mutual but falls short of our preferred position in three respects: (i) there is no carve-out permitting Corio to assign to an affiliate; (ii) the consent requirement has no reasonableness standard; and (iii) the competitor carve-back applies to both parties, so a merger, acquisition or asset sale involving a Commerce One competitor would require Commerce One's consent, letting the vendor block our exit. Section 11 contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing trigger, and no "change of control"/"deemed an assignment" language appears elsewhere, so only the assignment mechanics need fixing. The redline adds the affiliate carve-out, applies a "not unreasonably withheld or delayed" standard, and confines the competitor restriction to Commerce One's assignments.

quote: 2.1 Hosting Software License. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory to (i) reproduce the Software in machine executable object code format only for installation on the Corio Servers;
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation is imposed on Corio (our party), so the preferred position is already satisfied. Every license grant in Section 2 (2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4) and the escrow license in Section 12 is expressly "nonexclusive," and the Section 2.7 restrictions are ordinary IP scope and field-of-use limits (object code only, hosting on Corio Servers, no reverse engineering) rather than any commitment to source exclusively from Commerce One. There is no requirements language, minimum purchase commitment, "preferred/primary provider" designation, or covenant not to procure competing applications from third parties anywhere in the Agreement. Exhibit D's cross-selling, joint marketing and initial-customer provisions are introduced as "non-binding sales and marketing cooperation efforts" (p0198) and therefore create no enforceable exclusive dealing, and Section 13.6 affirmatively preserves each party's right to develop independently. Conversely, Section 2.4 grants exclusivity-style protection that runs in our favor (Commerce One may not contact Corio Customers regarding non-ASP license sales and must refer such Customers to Corio), which the rule expressly treats as acceptable and which we preserve. The other "exclusive" occurrences are unrelated boilerplate: fees being exclusive of taxes (4.3), Commerce One's sole and exclusive ownership warranty (7), Corio's sole and exclusive warranty remedies (7), and the entire-agreement clause (14). No redline is required.

quote: 11.3 Effect of Termination. The following Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 14.
rationale: Corio is the licensee/customer under this hosting and license agreement. Reviewing Fees (§4), Term and Termination (§11), Limitation of Liability (§9), Exhibit B Pricing/Revenue Sharing and Exhibit B Payment Terms, there is no liquidated damages provision, penalty, late-payment interest charge, minimum-fee commitment, early-termination fee or acceleration of unpaid fees payable by Corio. Termination under §11.2 simply ends the Agreement (with only ordinary continuing payment obligations for Customers Corio elects to keep supporting under §11.3), and §11.1 termination-for-convenience-on-notice at renewal carries no fee. Amounts flowing the other way (Commerce One's MarketSite transaction revenue share, and refunds of prepaid fees on acceptance-test failure or warranty breach under §3 and §7) benefit us and are compliant with the rule. The revenue share Corio pays to Commerce One under Exhibit B is usage-based consideration, not a liquidated damage or penalty. No redline required; the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) is already met.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a short provision extending the Section 2 licences to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (with us remaining responsible for their compliance), since our playbook requires licence scope to cover affiliates and contractors and the current grant is limited to Corio alone. If Commerce One prefers, we can accept coverage of Affiliates upon written notice as a fallback.

ops.text: 2.11 Affiliates and Contractors. The licenses granted to Corio under this Section 2 extend to Corio's Affiliates and to contractors acting on Corio's behalf, provided that Corio shall remain responsible for their compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement. For purposes of this Agreement, "AFFILIATE" means any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Corio, where "control" means direct or indirect ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of such entity.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 2 licences to Corio's Affiliates and to contractors acting on Corio's behalf

quote: 2.2 Internal Use License. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Commerce One grants to Corio a nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual right and license in the Territory to reproduce, install and use additional copies of the Software and Software tools and utilities
rationale: The grant is otherwise favourable to us: the hosting licence in Section 2.1 is "perpetual and irrevocable", the internal-use licence in Section 2.2 is perpetual and fully paid up, sublicensing to Customers is expressly permitted, and the nontransferability carve-out to Section 14.1 permits assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or asset sale. The one gap against our preferred position is the scope of licensed users: no licence rights run to Corio's affiliates or to contractors acting on Corio's behalf (the term "Affiliate" appears nowhere in the agreement), and the internal-use licence is confined to "Corio's internal business operations". We therefore propose a short new Section 2.11 extending the Section 2 licences to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, with Corio remaining responsible for their compliance.

quote: 13.6 Independent Development: Covenant not to Sue. Nothing in this Agreement will be construed to prohibit either parties' right to independently develop the Developments contemplated above.
rationale: No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant binds Corio (our party). Section 2.7 (p0042) restricts only copying/reverse engineering of Commerce One's Software, which is a standard IP protection rather than a business restraint; Sections 2.1–2.6 are grants in our favour, and 2.4 (p0035) plus 14.8 (p0131) expressly protect our freedom to resell and to subcontract. Section 13.6 (p0117) affirmatively preserves each party's right to develop independently, so nothing bars us from building, buying or hosting competing products. The "Territory" (p0024) and "Corio Market Segment" (p0013) definitions limit only the scope of the licence to Commerce One's own Software (and 2.10 obliges Commerce One not to unreasonably withhold worldwide expansion); they do not restrict what businesses we may operate or what products we may acquire. Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation is expressly "non-binding" (p0198) and contains no restraint on competing products. No redline required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11 locks us into a five-year term with exit only for material breach or insolvency, so we have added a customer right to terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' notice with a refund of prepaid fees, and confirmed Commerce One has no mid-term convenience exit. If thirty days is not workable, we can accept 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.text: 11.4 Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, without penalty, early termination fee or other charge, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio any prepaid fees covering the period after the effective date of such termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term.

proposal.summary: Add Corio termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; confirm no Commerce One convenience exit.

quote: 11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period.
rationale: Section 11.1 commits us to a five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals, and Section 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. There is no customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere in the Agreement (the only other exits are acceptance-test failure in 3.x and warranty/IP remedies in 7-8), which is a deviation under the rule for terms longer than 12 months. Commerce One likewise has no convenience right, which matches the preferred position, so the redline adds a new Section 11.4 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with a refund of prepaid fees and expressly confirms Commerce One has no mid-term convenience exit.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have tightened the audit mechanics to at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, our normal business hours, and an auditor who has signed a confidentiality undertaking, consistent with our position that audits be rare, notified and confidential; the existing annual cap and Commerce One cost allocation are unchanged. We can accept fifteen (15) days' notice as a fallback.

Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, during Corio's normal business hours and upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, and shall not include any access to Corio's systems or networks.
ops.oldText: an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio for the purpose of verifying the amounts payable to Commerce One under this Agreement. Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice.

proposal.summary: Specify 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, and auditor confidentiality undertaking in the § 4.4 audit right

quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit right binding Corio (our party). It already meets much of our position: once per calendar year, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, Commerce One bears costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no system access is granted. It deviates by leaving notice and timing as merely "reasonable" rather than a fixed 30 days' prior written notice during business hours, and by not requiring the auditor to be bound by confidentiality (the § 10 NDA binds only the parties, not their accountants). The redline adds those three items and confirms no access to our systems, without disturbing the agreed frequency or cost allocation.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced mandatory AAA arbitration with the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, retaining California law, because our position is that disputes be resolved in court rather than by binding arbitration. Our preferred position is New York law and the courts of New York County, but California courts are acceptable here given both parties are California-based.

ops.newText: Any disputes arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively in the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, and each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of those courts and waives any objection to venue or inconvenient forum therein.
ops.oldText: Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California. A judgment upon the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction of the parties, including without limitation the courts in San Francisco, California. The non-prevailing party in the arbitration shall pay all fees and charges of the American Arbitration Association; each party, however, shall be responsible for the payment of all fees and expenses connected with the presentation of its respective case.

proposal.summary: Replace mandatory AAA arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of California state and federal courts; retain California governing law.

quote: Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California.
rationale: Governing law is California, which is within the accepted list (and appropriate here as both parties are California-based), so the choice of law is compliant. However, the clause imposes mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration rather than resolution in court, which deviates from the playbook requirement for courts as the dispute forum. The arbitration seat is domestic (San Francisco), so this is not a walk-away issue. We took the fallback (California law and courts) rather than pushing New York, since the California-law bargain is reasonable for these parties; the minimal edit swaps the arbitration forum for exclusive jurisdiction of the San Francisco state and federal courts and conforms the heading.

quote: 2. Corio Customer Application Management Revenue: Corio to pay Commerce One [*] of all Application Management Revenue from Corio Customers for use of Commerce One Software or MarketSite.net Service Access subject to the following limitations.
rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation / best-pricing or price-parity obligation in either direction. Full-text searches for "most favo(u)red", "favorable/favourable", "no less favorable", "best price", "other customers", "similarly situated", "match" and related parity language returned nothing, and the commercial terms (Exhibit B Pricing at p0148–p0154, Revenue Sharing Fees at p0155–p0161, Payment Terms at sec-17, Fees at sec-4) are stated as fixed fees and revenue shares with no undertaking by Corio (our party, the licensee/customer) to extend Commerce One terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers. The Distribution License (2.4) and New Products (2.9) provisions likewise create no parity commitment — future product licensing is left to terms "as the parties may agree". The preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer) is therefore already met, so no redline is proposed. Note only that certain pricing figures in Exhibit B and in Section 2.4 are redacted ("[*]"); if any redacted term contains a pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking by Corio, this rule should be re-run against the unredacted text.

quote: SOFTWARE USERS: BuySite Hosted Edition: Unlimited
rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, or shortfall penalty is imposed on us (Corio). Exhibit B prices the licenses, MarketSite.net access and maintenance as fees for the services actually ordered (Sections 4.1-4.2, p0152-p0154), user volume is expressly "Unlimited" so there is no volume cap on our usage, revenue-sharing fees are a percentage of revenue actually invoiced to Corio Customers (p0157), and implementation work is time-and-materials with a cap (p0161). The only "minimum" references are a 40-Authorized-User floor that merely conditions the revenue-share exemption for the initial 3,000 licenses (p0158) and audit/true-up language in Section 4.4, which provides for payment of any "shortfall" or refund of overpayment rather than a penalty - consistent with the playbook's preferred true-up approach. Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation, including the initial-customers item, is expressly "non-binding" and effort-based, so it creates no purchase quota. The five-year initial term with annual fees is a term/exit issue addressed by the term and termination rules rather than a minimum commitment, so no redline is proposed here.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: 14.5 Independent Contractors. The parties are independent contractors with respect to each other. Each party is not and shall not be deemed to be an employee, agent, partner or legal representative of the other for any purpose and shall not have any right, power or authority to create any obligation or responsibility on behalf of the other.
rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binding Corio (our party). Literal searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce" returned no hits, and "employ" appears only in unrelated contexts: §13.5 (p0116) requires Commerce One personnel to sign Employee NDA/Invention Agreements, §14.5 (p0126) is a standard independent-contractor disclaimer, and Exhibit D ¶5 (p0203) merely requires each party to assign a sales/marketing employee to joint promotion. The candidate sections flagged by the planner (§13 Shared Resources and §14 Miscellaneous) were read in full and contain no restrictive covenant on hiring, notwithstanding the secondment of Commerce One operations, consulting and engineering personnel to work alongside Corio staff under §§13.1–13.3. This matches the playbook preferred position — no non-solicit on Customer — so no redline is required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The one-year auto-renewal and 30-day non-renewal notice work for us, but we have added a 60-day advance renewal reminder from Commerce One and a cap on renewal fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, consistent with our position that renewals be easy to exit and predictably priced. If a hard cap is an issue, we can accept a 5% ceiling.

ops.oldText: of its intention to terminate this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add vendor renewal reminder (60 days) and cap renewal fee increases at lesser of CPI and 3%

quote: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 11.1 already meets the preferred structure on renewal length (one-year renewals) and exit (30 days' notice, exercisable by Corio). However, it omits two preferred elements: a Commerce One reminder 60 days before each renewal, and any cap on renewal pricing. Exhibit B pricing (p0153-p0154) only states "Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]" and Section 4 contains no uplift limit, so renewal-term fee increases are uncapped. The redline adds the 60-day renewal reminder and caps renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5% fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a transition-assistance and data-return provision at Section 11.4: on exit, Commerce One provides up to six (6) months of migration assistance at its then-current rates, returns our and our Customers' data within thirty (30) days in a machine-readable format, and then deletes it and certifies deletion. Our playbook requires an orderly exit path for hosted services; we can accept ninety (90) days of assistance as a fallback, and have carved out retention needed for Commerce One's surviving support obligations and applicable law.

ops.text: 11.4 Transition Assistance and Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall, at Corio's request: (a) provide reasonable transition and migration assistance to Corio and its Customers for a period of up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current standard rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return to Corio all data of Corio and its Customers then in Commerce One's possession or control, including data generated through or stored in connection with the MarketSite.net Service, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing, except to the extent retention is required to perform Commerce One's surviving obligations under this Agreement or by applicable law. This Section 11.4 shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 11.4 requiring Commerce One to provide up to six months of transition assistance and to return, then delete and certify deletion of, Corio and Customer data on expiry or termination.

quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
rationale: Section 11 contains no transition-assistance or data-return obligation. Section 11.3 preserves Corio's customer-access rights and Commerce One's surviving support obligations, and Section 12 provides source code escrow, but nothing requires Commerce One to provide migration assistance on exit or to return Corio's and its Customers' data (including data held through the MarketSite.net Service) in a machine-readable format, or to delete and certify deletion thereafter. The generic Confidential Information "return or destroy" line in 11.3 is not a data-export right and could even support unilateral destruction of our data. As the hosting customer/licensee, we need the preferred exit protections, so we insert a new Section 11.4 with six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable data return, and deletion with written certification (subject to retention needed for surviving support obligations and law).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a warranty period that is meaningful in practice: 60 days measured from the Effective Date and capped at December 31, 1999 expires almost immediately and before most Customer deployments go live, so we have moved to twelve (12) months from delivery, kept the malicious-code warranty continuous, and added the standard professional and workmanlike warranty for the installation, implementation, support and professional services with a re-performance or refund remedy. If twelve months is not workable, we can accept ninety (90) days from delivery for the Software and thirty (30) days for services, with the same remedies.

ops.oldText: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")

ops.text: Services Warranty. Commerce One warrants that all installation, implementation, support, training and other professional services provided under this Agreement will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards. Corio's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Commerce One's option, prompt re-performance of the non-conforming services or a refund of the fees paid for such non-conforming services.

proposal.summary: Extend product warranty to 12 months from delivery, remove the fixed December 31, 1999 sunset, make the malicious-code warranty continuous, and add a professional-and-workmanlike services warranty with a re-performance/refund remedy.

quote: Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation, and the media on which the Software is distributed will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use, for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period").
rationale: Section 7.3 gives a conformance warranty but the duration falls below even the playbook fallback: sixty (60) days measured from the Effective Date (not delivery or acceptance) and hard-capped at December 31, 1999, so the warranty can expire before or immediately after deployment. The malicious-code warranty is also limited to that same short window and to "willfully introduced" code, and there is no professional-and-workmanlike warranty covering the installation, implementation, support, training and professional services under Section 5. The remedy in 7.3 (correction, replacement, and refund of prepaid fees on termination if not correctable) is acceptable, so the redline is limited to duration, continuous malicious-code coverage, and adding a services warranty with a re-performance/refund remedy. The disclaimer (p0084) addresses implied warranties only and does not swallow the express warranties, so no carve-out edit is needed.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a standard insurance covenant, as Commerce One personnel and contractors will access the Corio Servers and Corio and Customer data under Sections 13 and 5. Our playbook position is CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M and cyber liability of USD 5M where our data is processed, with certificates on request; we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

ops.text: 14.10 Insurance. Commerce One shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than one million U.S. dollars (US$1,000,000) per occurrence and two million U.S. dollars (US$2,000,000) in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than two million U.S. dollars (US$2,000,000); (c) where Commerce One processes, stores or has access to Corio's or its Customers' data, cyber liability insurance of not less than five million U.S. dollars (US$5,000,000); and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Commerce One shall provide Corio with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon Corio's request.

proposal.summary: Insert an insurance covenant on Commerce One in Miscellaneous (new Section 14.10) and renumber Complete Understanding.

quote: 14.9 Bankruptcy. The parties hereto agree that Corio, as a licensee of Commerce One's intellectual property, shall be afforded all of the protections afforded to a licensee under Section 365(n) of the United States Bankruptcy Code
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance clause (the only occurrence of "insurance" is in the Net Revenue definition), yet Commerce One operations, consulting and engineering personnel (and third-party integrators it may assign) work with Corio personnel on the hosted environment and may access Corio and Customer data. Playbook requires CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where our data is processed, workers' compensation and certificates on request, so we insert a short covenant as new Section 14.10 in Miscellaneous and renumber Complete Understanding.
